entry.summary: The origins of procurement date to around 3,000 BC when Egyptians were scribing orders for the two million limestone and granite blocks needed to build the Great Pyramid. By the 15th century, the first printing presses were publishing the first rudimentary sales catalogues and price lists. The Continental Congress of 1775, commissioning military supplies in New Jersey, was the first recorded use of advertising to solicit proposals. Napoleon introduced the world’s first formal legal procurement framework. Then in 1980 Margaret Thatcher introduced compulsory competitive tendering across UK civil construction.
